records.name: Cable Crunch
records.cues: Create the movement through spinal flexion and extension rather than bending at the hips.

records.name: Hanging Leg Raise
records.cues: Hang from a pull-up bar and raise the straight legs forward while slightly tucking the pelvis. Brace the torso to minimize swinging and control the eccentric.

records.name: Lying Leg Raise
records.cues: Lie on a bench or the floor and hold a support above the head. Raise the straight legs toward the torso and slightly lift the pelvis at the top. Lower slowly; add a dumbbell between the feet only if appropriate.

records.name: Machine Crunch
records.cues: Create the movement through spinal flexion and extension rather than bending at the hips.

records.name: Hip Adduction Machine
records.cues: Set the start position as wide as your mobility allows; use your hands to bring one pad inward if needed to enter safely. Anchor yourself with the handles and bring the knees together through the full range until the pads meet. Use partial repetitions only after full repetitions are no longer possible, and control the eccentric.

records.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
records.cues: Use a slight bench incline. Keep wrists straight and stacked over elbows, with the elbows angled slightly forward. Lower slowly to at least about 90 degrees or as far as mobility allows, without letting elbows fall behind the body or wrists collapse.

records.name: High-Incline Smith Machine Press
records.cues: Set the bench to about 70 degrees inside the Smith machine.

records.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
records.cues: Use two D-handles and set the cables around calf height so tension remains at full elbow extension. Stand stable with a slight forward torso lean. Keep the elbows fixed, curl from a fully extended position, and keep the wrists neutral and steady. Use a slow, controlled tempo.

records.name: Biceps Curl Machine
records.cues: Keep the upper arms and elbows pressed into the pad throughout, and maintain neutral, rigid wrists. Flex the elbows to raise the forearms, pressing the elbows into the pad, then control the eccentric.

records.name: Cable Curl
records.cues: Curl a straight or EZ bar in front of the body; use the straight bar only if it is comfortable for the wrists.

records.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
records.cues: Keep the dumbbells in a neutral grip throughout without rotating them. Curl only at the elbows while keeping elbows fixed and wrists straight. Reach full elbow extension at the bottom and use a slow tempo.

records.name: Preacher Curl
records.cues: Place the upper arms and elbows on the pad and hold a dumbbell or bar with neutral wrists. Keep the arms in contact with the pad as you curl from full extension, pressing the elbows into the support.

records.name: Straight-Bar Cable Curl
records.cues: Set the cable low enough to maintain tension at full elbow extension and stand facing the tower. Curl a straight bar with both hands while keeping elbows fixed and wrists neutral. Move slowly through full elbow flexion and extension.

records.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
records.cues: Place only the balls of the feet at the lower edge of the platform and keep the knees straight. Press through the forefoot to reach full ankle extension, then lower slowly into a deep calf stretch below neutral.

records.name: Seated Calf Raise
records.cues: Secure the thighs under the pad with the balls of the feet on the platform and heels free. Press through the forefoot to plantar-flex the ankles and raise the load, then lower slowly under control.

records.name: Single-Leg Standing Calf Raise (Band or Dumbbell)
Standing Calf Raise
records.cues: Place the balls of the feet on the platform with the heels free and keep the knees straight throughout. Press through the forefoot to extend the ankles and rise, then lower slowly under control.

records.name: Machine Chest Fly
records.cues: Set the seat so the handles align with the chest. Keep the torso upright, chest lifted, and shoulders down as the arms come together fully. Return only as far as shoulder mobility allows without the shoulders rising or collapsing, and keep the movement slow.

records.name: Reverse Banded High Incline Smith Press
Reverse Banded Low Incline Smith Press
Seated Cuffed Clavicular Pec Chest Press
Seated Cuffed Costal Pec Chest Press
Standing Cable Chest Fly
records.cues: Set the cables around shoulder height and use D-handles or cuffs. Stand securely with a slight forward lean. Maintain a small, fixed elbow bend while bringing the hands or handles together in front of the chest. Keep the torso tall, chest lifted, and shoulders down; control the return into a deep but comfortable stretch.

records.name: 45-Degree Back Extension (Glute Focus)
records.cues: Set the pad against the thighs so the hips can flex freely. Hold a plate or dumbbell with slightly bent arms and maintain slight spinal flexion rather than a rigid extended back. Drive the torso upward through hip extension from the glutes, avoid lumbar extension, and control the hip hinge on the way down.

records.name: B-Stance Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
records.cues: Place one foot slightly behind as a kickstand without loading it; keep nearly all weight on the front leg. Use one or two dumbbells depending on balance, and support yourself with the free hand if using one dumbbell. Push the hips back and lower the dumbbell along the outside of the working leg only as far as mobility allows. Keep the torso rigid and look down to maintain a neutral neck.

records.name: Barbell Good Morning
records.cues: Brace the torso, lightly retract the shoulder blades, and position the bar securely. From a narrow to hip-width stance, hinge at the hips by pushing them backward while the torso moves forward. Keep the spine rigid, stop at your available range, and move slowly.

records.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
records.cues: Pad the bar over the hips, support the upper back at shoulder-blade height, and set the feet flat so the knees reach about 90 degrees at the top. Drive through the heels to full hip extension while keeping the spine rigid rather than extending the lower back.

records.name: Barbell Lunge
records.cues: Position the bar so the torso can remain braced and neutral, with only a slight forward lean for balance. Place the working foot slightly in front of the bar and the nonworking leg diagonally behind for support only. Use a relatively short stride to maximize knee flexion, descend until the rear knee approaches the floor, then drive through the front foot to stand. Move slowly and keep the working knee stable.

records.name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
records.cues: Hinge at the hips by pushing them backward as the torso lowers. Keep the spine rigid, guide the bar close to the legs, lower only as far as mobility allows, and maintain a small knee bend.

records.name: Diagonal Cable Glute Kickback
records.cues: Set the cable low, use an ankle cuff, and elevate the stance foot slightly. Hinge forward while holding the tower overhead, then extend the working leg from a flexed position in a slightly externally rotated, diagonal backward path. Keep the movement controlled and driven by the glutes.

records.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat (Glute Focus)
records.cues: If possible, use a low Smith-machine bar with a pad as the rear-foot support. Hold one dumbbell opposite the working leg and use the free hand for balance. Place the working foot farther forward, allow a slight forward torso lean and hip hinge, and keep all load on the front leg. Descend deeply for a glute stretch, keep the dumbbell close to the working leg without resting it on the other leg, and move slowly.

records.name: Dumbbell Lunge
records.cues: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and step forward far enough to reach at least a 90-degree knee angle; a smaller angle creates more knee flexion and quadriceps emphasis. Keep most of the load on the front leg, use the rear leg only for balance, and allow a slight forward torso lean. Lower under control, drive through the front foot to return, and keep the knees tracking steadily without collapsing inward or outward.

records.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
records.cues: Hinge at the hips by pushing them backward as the torso lowers. Keep the spine rigid, lower only as far as mobility allows, and guide the dumbbells close to the legs. A small knee bend is acceptable; use a slow tempo and pause briefly in the stretch.

records.name: Glute Kickback Machine
records.cues: Support the torso on the pad and place the working foot on the platform. Drive the foot into the platform to extend the leg, reaching full extension at the top and a deep controlled bend at the bottom. Keep the tempo slow.

records.name: Hip Thrust Machine
records.cues: Position the pad over the hips and the feet flat so the knees reach about 90 degrees at the top. Drive through the heels to full hip extension while keeping the spine and torso rigid rather than extending the lower back. Control the eccentric.

records.name: Leg Press - High Wide Stance
records.cues:
• Anchor yourself firmly in the seat and place the feet high and wide on the platform. Bend the knees as deeply as possible while keeping them stable and tracking outward. Drive through the feet to extend, and keep both phases slow and controlled.
 • Use a high, wide stance, enter the movement cautiously, and take about three seconds on the eccentric.

records.name: Single-Leg Barbell Hip Thrust
records.cues: Pad the bar over the hips and support the upper back at shoulder-blade height. With one foot flat and the knee near 90 degrees at the top, drive through the heel to full hip extension. Keep the torso and spine rigid rather than extending the lower back.

records.name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat (Glute Focus)
Smith Machine Hip Thrust
records.cues: Pad the bar over the hips, support the upper back at shoulder-blade height, and set the feet flat so the knees reach about 90 degrees at the top. Drive through the heels to full hip extension while keeping the spine rigid. Begin from the top position when setting up because it is easier.

records.name: Smith Machine Lunge
records.cues: Set up under the bar so the torso can stay upright, braced, and neutral. Place the working foot slightly in front of the bar and move the nonworking leg behind for balance only. Keep the stride relatively short to emphasize knee flexion, descend until the rear knee approaches the floor, and drive through the front foot to stand. Move slowly and keep the front knee stable without collapsing inward.

records.name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
records.cues: Hinge at the hips by pushing them backward as the torso lowers. Keep the spine rigid, use only a small knee bend, lower only as far as mobility allows, and move slowly.

records.name: Straight-Leg Cable Glute Kickback
records.cues: Set the cable low, attach an ankle cuff, and stand upright while holding the tower. Elevate the stance foot if needed and move the working leg straight backward without bending the knee or moving the torso. Use a slow, controlled tempo.

records.name: Behind-The-Body Cable Kickback (Gluteus Medius)
records.cues: Set the cable low and attach an ankle cuff. Stand upright while holding the tower, with the stance leg slightly in front of the working leg. Move the working leg diagonally backward from beside the body. Keep the torso still, the knees unbent, and perform the movement slowly from the glutes.

records.name: Cable Hip Abduction
records.cues: Set the cable at ankle height and attach the outer leg with a cuff while standing side-on to the tower. Step far enough away to keep tension at the start while retaining support with the near hand. Move the working leg laterally with a small fixed knee bend, keeping the limb rigid and the load light enough for full range.

records.name: Hip Abduction Machine
records.cues: Pull yourself firmly into the seat; use straps if needed. Press the outsides of the knees into the pads and drive the legs away from the body. Add padding between the legs and pads if needed to increase range. Move slowly, pause briefly at full abduction, and keep the torso neutral or slightly forward.

records.name: Barbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
records.cues: Begin with only a slight hip bend, then lower the rigid torso primarily through hamstring lengthening. Keep the knees fixed, the bar moving straight down rather than tracing the legs, and the spine neutral. Descend only as far as the hamstrings allow and use straps if needed.

records.name: Lying Leg Curl
records.cues: Press the hips firmly into the pad and keep the torso and thighs still. Curl the lower legs fully toward the hamstrings, then return slowly to full knee extension without lifting the hips.

records.name: Seated Leg Curl
records.cues: Align the knee joint with the machine pivot and pull yourself firmly into the seat. Keep the thighs still while curling the lower legs toward the hamstrings. Control the eccentric and finish with full knee extension.

records.name: Single-Leg Kneeling Leg Curl
records.cues: Press the working knee and thigh firmly into the pad. Curl the lower leg fully toward the hamstrings while keeping the hip stable, then return slowly to extension.

records.name: Standing Leg Curl
records.cues: Press the working thigh and knee firmly into the pad while curling the lower leg toward the hamstrings. Do not let the thigh lift; return slowly to full knee extension.

records.name: Cable Y-Raise
records.cues: Set both cables around hip height, cross them, and attach cuffs to the opposite wrists. Stand slightly forward of the tower and keep the body still. Raise both arms outward and slightly forward in a Y path, keeping wrists below the elbows. Move slowly and add controlled partials if desired.

records.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
records.cues: Raise the slightly bent arms laterally, keeping wrists aligned with and no higher than the elbows. Avoid excessive body momentum and drive the movement from the lateral deltoids. Controlled partial repetitions may be added near the end.

records.name: Machine Lateral Raise
records.cues: Set the seat so the lateral deltoids sit just below the pads and brace the torso against the support. Press the slightly bent arms into the pads and raise them laterally and slightly forward. Control the eccentric; partial repetitions may be added near the end.

records.name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
records.cues: Set the cable around hip height and use a cuff. Stand tall, hold the tower with the near arm, and raise the working arm laterally while keeping the elbow and wrist aligned. Avoid body momentum; controlled partials may be added near the end.

records.name: Bent-Over Barbell Row - Supinated Grip (Latissimus Focus)
records.cues: Use a hip-width stance with a moderate forward torso lean and neutral spine. From straight arms and a slightly narrower-than-shoulder-width underhand grip, pull the bar toward the hips using the lats. Avoid lower-body momentum and move slowly.

records.name: Chin-Up (Supinated Grip)
records.cues:
• Use a shoulder-width or narrower supinated grip so the path stays close to the body. Pull up without letting the shoulders roll inward at the top. At the bottom, keep lat tension rather than hanging completely relaxed. Move slowly and use straps if needed.
 • Use rings or freely rotating handles if available.

records.name: Close-Grip Supinated MAG Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Sit neutrally with only a slight upright posture and no excessive backward lean. From straight arms and controlled shoulders, pull the handle to the upper chest while driving the elbows toward the hips and keeping them close to the body. Move slowly.

records.name: Hammer Strength Row (Latissimus Focus)
records.cues: Set the seat so the chest is supported and the shoulders can remain neutral. Pull the elbows from extension toward the hips, keeping the path close to the body. Control the eccentric and stop the stretch before the shoulders roll forward or lat tension is lost.

records.name: Hammer Strength Single-Arm Supinated Pulldown
records.cues: Perform one arm at a time and pull the elbow toward the same-side hip.

records.name: High Cable Row (Latissimus)
records.cues: Sit on an elevated support and use a shoulder-width grip.

records.name: Lat Prayer Pullover
records.cues: Review the demonstration video before performing the exercise.

records.name: Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Use a standard bar and roughly shoulder-width grip. Sit tall with only a slight backward lean and pull the bar toward the upper chest. Reach full elbow extension while maintaining shoulder control, avoid swinging or excessive torso lean, and control the return.

records.name: Medium Neutral-Grip MAG Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Keep the torso neutral and still without exaggerated extension or rounding. Pull by driving the elbows toward the hips, keep the shoulders controlled, and avoid using momentum from a backward lean.

records.name: Medium Supinated-Grip MAG Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Keep a neutral torso and look forward. Initiate from the lats and pull the elbows toward the hips. Return slowly without over-stretching or letting the shoulders roll out of position, and do not lean backward for momentum.

records.name: Rope Cable Pullover
records.cues: Set the cable overhead and hinge the torso slightly forward. With the arms held in a fixed position, pull the rope from above the head toward the hips using the lats. Keep the rope path close and avoid spreading the ends outward; a small torso rise is acceptable.

records.name: Seated Cable Row - Shoulder-Width Grip (Latissimus)
records.cues: Sit with a neutral torso and slight forward lean. From straight arms while retaining lat tension, pull the elbows toward the hips and keep them close to the body. Bring the handle close without rocking the torso, control the return, and use straps if needed.

records.name: Single-Arm Cable Iliac Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Set the cable high and diagonally, use a D-handle, and brace the free arm on a moderately inclined bench. Hold the working hand in slight external rotation and keep the grip fixed. Pull the elbow toward the hip along a path close to the body, using a slow, controlled tempo.

records.name: Single-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Use a D-handle and pull the working elbow toward the same-side hip while keeping the torso stable.

records.name: Single-Arm Cable Pullover
records.cues: Set the cable overhead and hinge the torso forward. Hold the cable above the head with one arm and pull toward the hip while keeping the arm straight or only slightly bent in a fixed position. Move slowly and under control.

records.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row (Latissimus Focus)
records.cues: Drive the elbow toward the hip.

records.name: Single-Arm Seated Cable Row (Latissimus Focus)
records.cues: Use a D-handle with a slightly externally rotated hand and keep that grip fixed. Maintain a neutral torso with a small forward and working-side lean. Keep the arm close to the body, pull the elbow toward the hip, allow full controlled extension, and avoid wrist rotation.

records.name: Standing Hammer Strength Row
records.cues: Stand behind the machine and brace with the nearly straight nonworking arm. Pull the handle close to the body by driving the elbow toward the hip. Reach full extension under control and use straps if needed.

records.name: Standing Single-Arm Hammer Strength Row
records.cues: Stand behind the seat and brace the nonworking arm on the chest pad, using the seat for lower-body support if needed. Keep a neutral torso with a slight lean toward the working side and use the narrower handle. Pull the elbow toward the hip along a close path, control the return, and use straps if needed.

records.name: Supinated Smith Machine Incline Bench Row
V-Bar Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Sit upright with a neutral spine and no backward swing. Pull the handle from straight arms to the upper chest while keeping the elbows close and driving them toward the hips. Control both phases and use straps if needed.

records.name: Wide-Grip MAG Lat Pulldown
records.cues: Sit tall and use a very wide grip. Pull the bar from straight arms to the upper chest without leaning backward or generating momentum from the torso.

records.name: Decline Chest Press Machine
records.cues: Set the seat so the handles align with the chest and choose a width that stacks wrists over elbows in the stretched position. Retract the shoulder blades, keep the shoulders down and chest lifted, then press forward from the deepest controlled stretch. Keep wrists neutral and control the eccentric without letting the shoulders rise.

records.name: Flat Barbell Bench Press
records.cues: Use a slight natural arch, retract the shoulder blades, and keep the shoulders down. Choose a grip that keeps wrists stacked over elbows at the bottom. Lower the bar from near lockout to the chest under control, without hyperextending the elbows, flaring excessively, or letting the wrists bend.

records.name: Flat Dumbbell Bench Press
records.cues: Use a standard flat dumbbell bench press setup. Tuck the elbows slightly and think about bringing them together in front of the body while pressing. Keep the back firmly against the bench.

records.name: Horizontal Chest Press Machine
records.cues: Set the seat so the handles align with the chest and wrists stack over elbows in the stretch. Retract the shoulder blades, keep the shoulders down and chest lifted, and maintain neutral wrists. Press forward and return into the deepest comfortable stretch without elbow or shoulder collapse.

records.name: Push-Up
records.cues: Set the hands around shoulder width or slightly wider with the body fully braced. Lower slowly until the chest nearly reaches the floor, then press the floor away. Keep the shoulders controlled and the body rigid throughout.

records.name: Cross-Body Cable Reverse Fly
records.cues: Set the cables above shoulder height and grasp the opposite cable with each hand. Keep wrists straight and arms slightly bent as the posterior deltoids move the arms diagonally backward. Keep the shoulders down and move slowly.

records.name: Hammer Strength Row (Posterior Deltoid Focus)
records.cues: Use a lower seat so the elbows travel outward and back and the shoulder blades retract. Allow the shoulders to reach forward at the stretch without shrugging. Keep the chest mostly on the pad and control both directions.

records.name: Reverse Fly Machine
records.cues: Set the seat so the handles align with the shoulders. Keep the neck and torso neutral, and hold the arms straight or with a small fixed elbow bend. Move the arms backward using the posterior deltoids and shoulder-blade retraction, with a slow, controlled tempo.

records.name: Barbell Back Squat
records.cues: Place the bar on the muscular shelf rather than directly on the spine, brace the torso, and grip close enough for stability. Choose a stance that allows stable, pain-free knee and hip tracking. Descend with coordinated hip and knee flexion to at least about 90 degrees, keep the torso balanced over the feet, and rise under control. Consider a belt for heavy loads.

records.name: Belt Squat
records.cues: Stand about hip-width directly above the belt attachment with a neutral, braced torso, and position the belt above the hip bones. Lead the descent with knee flexion, aiming for at least 90 degrees and more if mobility permits, while limiting excessive hip travel. Drive through the feet to stand without pulling on the supports unless needed to finish the final repetitions. Move slowly and under control.

records.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat (Quadriceps Focus)
records.cues: If possible, use a low Smith-machine bar with a pad as the rear-foot support. Hold one dumbbell opposite the working leg and use the free hand for balance. Elevate the front heel if available and position the foot close enough to maximize knee flexion. Keep all load on the working leg, descend as deeply as possible, and move slowly without resting the dumbbell on the other leg.

records.name: Hack Squat
records.cues: Use the lowest and narrowest stance your anatomy allows to maximize knee flexion. Keep the torso supported and the knees stable, descend under control, and drive the full foot into the platform to stand. Inhale during the descent, exhale on the ascent, and use a belt when loads become heavy if appropriate.

records.name: Lying Hack Squat
records.cues: Use the lowest and narrowest stance your anatomy allows and set the machine for maximum comfortable knee flexion. Press the shoulders and torso into the pad with a neutral spine, keep the knees stable, descend slowly, and drive the feet into the platform to extend.

records.name: Pendulum Squat
records.cues: Place the feet flat on the platform in the deepest, narrowest stable stance your mobility allows. Press the torso firmly into the back pad, keep the knees tracking steadily, and descend to maximize knee flexion. Drive through the feet to extend, inhale on the descent, exhale on the ascent, and control the eccentric.

records.name: Reverse V-Squat
records.cues: Face the back pad under the shoulder supports with a braced, neutral torso. Use a flat, hip-width stance close enough to remain upright. Descend to maximize knee flexion while limiting unnecessary hip travel, then drive through the feet to extend. Move slowly and under control.

records.name: Seated Leg Extension Machine
records.cues: Pull yourself firmly into the seat, using straps if helpful. Set the machine to allow maximum comfortable knee flexion; add padding between the shins and roller if needed. Extend through the knees and control the full movement.

records.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
records.cues: Place one foot flat and neutral on the platform, using a low stance to maximize knee flexion. Anchor yourself in the seat, keep the knee stable, descend deeply, and drive through the foot to extend.

records.name: Sissy Squat
records.cues: Adjust the sissy-squat support so the knees can reach maximum comfortable flexion over the pad. Lean back over the support as the knees bend, then press the shins and hamstrings into the pad to return to extension. Move slowly.

records.name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat (Quadriceps Focus)
Smith Machine Squat
records.cues: Place the bar on the muscular shelf rather than directly on the spine, brace the shoulder blades, and grip near the shoulders. Use a relatively narrow stance close enough to the machine to maximize knee flexion without the lower back rounding. Descend slowly, inhale on the way down, and drive through the feet while exhaling to stand.

records.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
records.cues: Start with the bar on the floor, shins close to it, feet about hip-width, and the torso braced with a neutral spine. Think of pressing the floor away as the bar rises close to the legs. Look down enough to keep the neck neutral, use straps if appropriate, and consider a belt for heavier loads.

records.name: Bilateral Cross-Body Cable Triceps Pushdown
records.cues: Set both cables above shoulder height so tension remains in the flexed position and grasp the opposite cable with each hand. Stand upright and stable. Keep elbows fixed while moving only through elbow flexion and extension, and keep wrists neutral and rigid.

records.name: Cable Katana Triceps Extension
records.cues: Set the cables low, face away from the tower, and cross the cables behind the back into a two-arm overhead position. Keep elbows beside the head and fixed while extending and flexing only at the elbows. Keep wrists neutral and maximize the comfortable stretch.

records.name: Close-Grip Smith Machine Bench Press
records.cues: Lie neutrally on a flat bench and use a grip narrower than shoulder width but not so narrow that the hands touch. Keep wrists and elbows stable while moving through elbow flexion and extension. Maximize comfortable elbow flexion and control the eccentric.

records.name: Dumbbell Overhead Triceps Extension
records.cues: Sit on a bench with the upper arm beside the head. Keep the elbow fixed and wrist neutral as the forearm lowers into deep elbow flexion, then extend smoothly. Move slowly and under control.

records.name: Parallel-Bar Dip
records.cues: Use handles that keep the arms reasonably close to the torso. Start at elbow extension, descend under control to at least about 90 degrees, then press back up. Keep the shoulders neutral and stop before they collapse forward; keep the elbows tracking consistently.

records.name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
records.cues: Set the cable above the head and face the tower with a slight forward body position. Hold the ends of the rope, keep wrists straight and elbows fixed, and move only through elbow flexion and extension. Use a slow, controlled tempo.

records.name: Single-Arm Overhead Cable Triceps Extension
records.cues: Set the cable around knee height and hold a cuff in the hand. Keep the wrist neutral and the elbow fixed throughout. Lower the forearm slowly into the deepest comfortable elbow flexion, then extend without moving the upper arm.

records.name: Triceps Dip Machine
records.cues:
• Use the dip machine and form a V shape with the hands, similar to a diamond push-up.
 • Set the seat so the handles begin slightly high and the wrists finish below the elbows at extension. Secure yourself with the belt or thigh pad. Bend the elbows as deeply as your shoulders allow while keeping the shoulders down; stop if they begin to rise or collapse. Move slowly and under control.

records.name: Bench-Supported Single-Arm Dumbbell Row (Upper Back Focus)
Bent-Over Barbell Row - Pronated Grip (Upper Back Focus)
records.cues: Use a stable hip-width stance and hinge the torso forward with a neutral spine. From straight arms and a shoulder-width overhand grip, initiate with the shoulder blades and upper back to row the bar toward the chest. Control the eccentric and avoid using lower-body momentum.

records.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row (Upper Back Focus)
records.cues: Hinge the torso forward and maintain roughly a 90-degree hip angle. Let the upper arms travel downward in front of the body, then row them outward toward the navel.

records.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row (Upper Back Focus)
records.cues: Set an incline bench high enough that the arms can hang without touching the floor. Position the chest so the shoulder blades can protract fully at the bottom. From straight arms, retract the shoulder blades and row with the elbows moving outward from the torso. Move slowly and use straps if needed.

records.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
records.cues:
• Set up so the shoulders can reach a full forward stretch. Initiate the row with the shoulder blades and upper back, pulling the elbows outward toward the body rather than keeping them tucked. Keep the grip stable without rotating it.
 • Set up with enough room to let the shoulder blades reach a full stretch at the bottom. Initiate the row from the upper back and shoulder blades; a small lift of the chest from the pad at the top is acceptable. Control the eccentric and use straps if needed.
 • Use a chest-supported setup if available.

records.name: High Row
records.cues: Keep the chest lifted and torso upright. Initiate from the shoulder blades, pulling the elbows toward you and outward rather than tucking them against the body. Move slowly and under control.

records.name: Low Row Machine (Upper Back Focus)
records.cues: Set the seat so the torso is above the handles and pull upward from below toward the body, keeping the elbows close. Move slowly and use straps if needed.

records.name: Pronated Smith Machine Incline Bench Row
Seated Cable Row - Pronated Wide-Grip (Upper Back Focus)
records.cues: Sit upright and take a fairly wide overhand grip. From straight arms, initiate with shoulder-blade retraction and pull the bar toward the chest with elbows moving outward. Avoid torso momentum, control the return, and use straps if needed.

records.name: T-Bar Bent-Over Row
records.cues: Use a stable hip-width stance with the torso hinged forward. Initiate from the shoulder blades and upper back, rowing the bar toward the chest. Reach a full controlled stretch at the bottom without using momentum from the lower body.

records.name: Incline Chest Press
records.cues: Lie on the incline with a slight natural arch, shoulder blades retracted, shoulders down, and chest lifted. Whether using a barbell or machine, keep wrists aligned over elbows. Lower to a deep but controlled stretch at the upper chest, stopping before the elbows or shoulders collapse, then press smoothly.

records.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
records.cues: Use a low-to-moderate incline and position the elbows slightly forward of the shoulders rather than directly out to the sides. Keep wrists stacked over elbows and both joints stable. Lower slowly to at least about a 90-degree elbow angle or deeper if comfortable, then press to arm extension without bringing the dumbbells together.

records.name: Low-Incline Smith Machine Bench Press
records.cues: Use the first incline setting, a slight natural arch, retracted shoulder blades, and shoulders held down. Choose a grip that stacks wrists over elbows at the bottom. Lower the bar toward the upper chest under control, avoid elbow flare or wrist collapse, and stop just short of elbow hyperextension at the top.
